content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: CheckoutViewModel stores all six delivery fields in plain mutableStateOf properties (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), which are only in process memory. The screen reads and writes them directly (CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72), and it creates the ViewModel via the default viewModel() with no saved-state handle (CheckoutScreen.kt:34). When Android kills the background process, the ViewModel is discarded, and on relaunch a new instance starts with every field blank, which is exactly the observed loss. Because the isComplete gate (CheckoutViewModel.kt:26-27) then disables Place order, the user has to retype everything.
Fix approach: Take a SavedStateHandle in the ViewModel constructor and back each field with it, for example with handle.getStateFlow or a mutableStateOf-backed saved key via a getter/setter that writes to handle["name"]. The default viewModel() factory injects the handle automatically, so CheckoutScreen.kt needs no change. The form then survives process death through the saved-state bundle, and the existing property names keep the screen code unchanged.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13 - class CheckoutViewModel : ViewModel() takes no SavedStateHandle; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19 - the six delivery fields are plain mutableStateOf("") and are not saved anywhere; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:26-27 - isComplete depends on those in-memory fields, so Place order stays disabled after the fields are lost; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel() with no saved-state setup; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - the screen reads and writes the form directly through vm.name, vm.email, and so on, so the loss reaches the UI

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test CheckoutViewModelSavedStateTest in src/test. It creates CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle()), sets name='Ravi Kumar', email, phone, address, city and pincode, then copies the handle's saved state (handle.savedStateProvider().saveState()) into a new SavedStateHandle and constructs a second CheckoutViewModel from it. It asserts all six properties equal the originally entered values and isComplete is true. Before the fix this fails: the constructor does not accept a handle, and the restored fields are blank.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.SavedStateHandle
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class CheckoutViewModelSavedStateTest {
    @Test
    fun formSurvivesProcessDeath() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val original = CheckoutViewModel(handle).apply {
            name = "Ravi Kumar"
            email = "ravi@example.com"
            phone = "9876543210"
            address = "12 MG Road"
            city = "Bengaluru"
            pincode = "560001"
        }

        val restoredHandle = SavedStateHandle(handle.keys().associateWith { handle.get<Any>(it) })
        val restored = CheckoutViewModel(restoredHandle)

        assertEquals(original.name, restored.name)
        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", restored.name)
        assertEquals("ravi@example.com", restored.email)
        assertEquals("9876543210", restored.phone)
        assertEquals("12 MG Road", restored.address)
        assertEquals("Bengaluru", restored.city)
        assertEquals("560001", restored.pincode)
        assertTrue(restored.isComplete)
    }
}

content.text:
I fixed the lost checkout form in `CheckoutViewModel.kt`, and the unit-test source set compiles. I haven't run the new test.

`CheckoutViewModel` now takes a `SavedStateHandle`, with an empty handle as the default so the existing `CheckoutViewModelTest` still constructs it. Each of the six delivery fields is backed by a private `SavedField` delegate. It keeps the same Compose state as before and also writes every change into the handle, so the form survives process death. The public property names are unchanged, so `CheckoutScreen.kt` needs no edit.

The regression test is `CheckoutViewModelSavedStateTest`. It deviates from your spec in one way: instead of `savedStateProvider().saveState()`, it copies the handle's keys into a new `SavedStateHandle` and builds a second view model from that. That call returns an Android `Bundle`, which JVM unit tests can't use without Robolectric, and the project doesn't have it. The test then asserts all six values match and `isComplete` is true.
